2607.24667.title: Eviction as Estimation: A Fixed-Lag Smoothing View of Test-Time Memory, and When Measuring Beats Accumulating
2607.24667.paper_summary: A language model with a bounded working memory must repeatedly decide which stored items to keep. Every deployed method decides the moment an item arrives, from the past (StreamingLLM, H2O) or from a guess about the future (SnapKV). We recast the choice as an estimation problem on a hidden signal, whether an item will be reused, placing existing methods on one axis, the commit lag $H$: online filters and learned predictors commit at $H=0$, while Belady's offline optimum sits where the whole future is known. The missing regime in between, fixed-lag smoothing, waits a bounded number of steps, observes which items a correct near-future prediction attended to, and only then commits. This measurement, demonstrated utility, turns Belady's unobservable future request into something we read off the model itself. We instantiate it as a training-free policy, RMM, a strict generalization of H2O that reduces to it exactly when the measurement is uniform. In controlled settings where reuse is endogenous and separated in time, demonstrated utility identifies used memory far better than accumulated attention, and a small bounded memory behaves like a much larger one. But on independent third-party benchmarks, run inside NVIDIA's KVPress harness against its own SnapKV, H2O, and StreamingLLM implementations, the advantage mostly disappears: RMM is on par with H2O for single-turn question answering and loses to both H2O and SnapKV in a streaming multi-turn setting. The cause is simple: on natural text the model is correct about most tokens, so weighting attention by correctness barely changes it, and demonstrated utility collapses onto accumulated attention unless reuse is sharp and endogenous, which standard benchmarks do not exercise. Our contribution is the framework and an honest map of when measuring beats accumulating, not a new state of the art.
2607.24667.paper_summary_zh: 一個具有有限工作記憶的語言模型必須不斷決定保留哪些存儲項目。每種部署的方法在項目到達的瞬間做出決定，無論是來自過去（StreamingLLM，H2O）還是對未來的猜測（SnapKV）。我們將這個選擇重新表述為一個隱藏信號的估計問題，即某個項目是否會被重用，將現有方法放在一個軸上，承諾延遲 $H$：在線過濾器和學習預測器在 $H=0$ 時承諾，而 Belady 的離線最佳則位於整個未來都是已知的地方。中間缺失的範疇，固定延遲平滑，等待有限步數，觀察正確的近未來預測所關注的項目，然後才進行承諾。這一測量，顯示出的效用，將 Belady 的不可觀察未來請求轉化為我們從模型本身讀取的東西。我們將其實例化為一個無需訓練的策略 RMM，這是一個 H2O 的嚴格泛化，當測量是均勻時恰好縮減為它。在可控的環境中，當重用是內生的並且時間上分開時，顯示的效用比累積注意力更好地識別使用的記憶，而小的有限記憶表現得像一個更大的記憶。但在獨立的第三方基準測試中，運行在 NVIDIA 的 KVPress 環境中，與其自己的 SnapKV、H2O 和 StreamingLLM 實現相比，這一優勢大多消失：RMM 在單輪問題回答中與 H2O 不相上下，但在流式多輪設定中輸給了 H2O 和 SnapKV。原因很簡單：在自然文本中，模型對大多數標記是正確的，因此根據正確性加權注意力幾乎不會改變它，而顯示的效用會崩潰到累積注意力上，除非重用是尖銳且內生的，而標準基準測試並未進行這方面的測試。我們的貢獻是這一框架以及一個誠實的地圖，說明何時測量優於累積，而不是一種新的技術前沿。
2607.24667.author: Maruthi Vemula et.al.
